Getting started

Prerequisites

Obtain a local checkout of paulweezydesign/f and open a terminal in its root directory, next to package.json . Installation and the baseline build were verified with Node.js 22.23.2 and npm 10.9.8. This records the tested environment, not a claim that every Node.js version is supported.

The first installation needs access to the npm registry. Keep package-lock.json so installs use the repository's locked dependency versions.

Quick start

npm ci
npm start

npm start builds the site, starts the source watcher, and launches BrowserSync against dist/ . Open the local preview address printed in your terminal, then follow the Documentation link or append /docs/index.html to that address. Stop the preview with Ctrl+C.

This project uses an older locked toolchain. Review installation warnings rather than assuming that a successful build means every dependency is secure. Do not run force upgrades as part of ordinary setup.

Edit the source

Change src/pug/index.pug for the landing page, src/pug/docs/ for these guides, or src/scss/styles.scss for styles. Existing pages rebuild when their source changes. Restart npm start after adding new Pug pages so later shared-layout edits include them in the watcher's page registry.

Do not keep your only copy of changes in dist/ : the next full build deletes and recreates that directory. See the migration guide if you already edited generated files.

Build and validate

npm run build
npm run test:docs

The full build cleans dist/ and compiles all pages, styles, scripts, and assets. The documentation check validates the generated pages and local links. npm test runs the build and documentation check together.

Publish

Preview the output, then upload the entire dist/ directory to your static host. Keep docs/ , css/ , js/ , and assets/ in their generated locations. Review both the template and documentation at the actual deployment path before making the site public.
